why: The statement is a single universal claim. Results about how often orbits behave (Terras, Korec, Krasikov–Lagarias, Tao) and minimum cycle-length results (Simons–de Weger, Hercher) are answered as bound, since they move a proportion or a smallest-possible-counterexample size and leave the question open. Inselmann's natural-density improvement of Korec's exponent is the one bound after the snapshot. The density results in Chang 2603.11066 (density-0 divergence, almost-all convergence) were already known from Terras and Tao. What is new there is a spectral-gap framework and a diagnosis of why the problem resists proof, so I answered none rather than bound. That was the closest call. If it were a bound, its AI role, assisted on the abstract's co-production credit, would enter at the progress tier. Reductions, frameworks, conditional results and verification algorithms are none. Bařina's check up to 2^71 and the random-sample checks are instances. The Bouhamidi families and antihydra are variants. The CollatzLean disproof is knocked down by the kernel-bug postmortem. Its AI involvement is unnamed and its systems list is empty, so its AI role is none. The many self-published proof claims, and the uncorroborated OpenAI report, each show several F10 signals and are not_credible. wrc-lean is AI-generated, but it proves nothing about termination.
doubts: Chang 2603.11066's Section 12 was not read, so its AI role (assisted) rests on the abstract's co-production statement alone. It is moot under scope none. Whether the near-universal density results count as bounds on this statement is a judgement call; I treated measure of exceptions as a bound quantity throughout. Hercher's journal acceptance is taken as digestion despite the corrigendum. The Bouhamidi HAL 2024 entry gives only a year, so its date is null.
